compiled_state.author: Joe Oakhart
compiled_state.description:
An execution row carries a state such as REVIEW or IMPLEMENTING with no indication of whether the backing Temporal workflow is still live. The same value means two different things. When the workflow is live the run is genuinely in that stage. When the workflow has closed the row is awaiting the orphan reclaimer, which flips it to CANCELLED on the next intake pass once execution_orphan_grace_seconds has elapsed.

Reading the row alone, an operator cannot tell an active run from one that ended and has not yet been reconciled, so a completed-but-unreconciled execution reads as stuck. This produced a false defect report during the massgov pilot.

The disambiguating facts already exist. Workflow liveness is available from Temporal, and the terminal alert carries the reason, for example REVIEW_BLOCKED with blocking gate acceptance, but it is only written to worker logs.

Surface liveness and the last terminal alert next to the state wherever executions are reported, so the distinction between in progress, blocked, and awaiting reconciliation is visible without reading worker logs.
compiled_state.title: ADEVX-120 Surface workflow liveness alongside execution state
